Verdict: REVISEThe mathematical core is sound, and the three-source family is a genuine all-parameter witness once its parity and phase adapters are made explicit. I found no counterexample to the coordinate construction, the  $h+4\le a$  bound, or the claimed refutation of
$$\text{full forced receiver}\Longrightarrow
\text{the forced point occupies a }P_{\mathrm{neg}}\text{ slot}.$$
I would not mark the supplied artifact as unconditional ACCEPT yet, because the formal file proves a conditional arithmetic predicate, while the physical statement still depends on an unproved adapter from “phase10  $U$ -ownership at the transported forced point” to that predicate. There are also two scope and wording corrections that should be made.If those adapters are already independently accepted premises in the preceding theory, then the mathematical result itself is acceptable after the editorial corrections below.1. Universal phase10 role classificationThe formal theoremleanphase_ten_forced_owner_is_north_terminalis exhaustive relative to its stated hypotheses.The canonical endpoint predicate has exactly the three necessary cases:
$$\begin{aligned}
&\text{bar: }0\le r\le1,\quad 1\le c\le w,\\
&\text{near leg: }c=1,\quad 2\le r\le \ell,\\
&\text{far leg: }c=w,\quad 2\le r\le r'.
\end{aligned}$$
The three orientation bits  $(\mathsf{transpose},\mathsf{flipRow},\mathsf{flipColumn})$  enumerate all eight signed coordinate permutations. The four blocker hypotheses exclude the four foreign endpoints
$$(0,-1),\quad (1,0),\quad (-1,-1),\quad (1,1)$$
in the normalized frame. Under the parity predicate
$$r\bmod 2=
\begin{cases}
1,&\mathsf{flipRow},\\
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad
c\bmod 2=
\begin{cases}
0,&\mathsf{flipColumn},\\
1,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}$$
the only surviving cases are exactly
$$\begin{aligned}
&\mathsf{transpose}=\mathsf{false},\quad
\mathsf{flipRow}=\mathsf{false},\quad
\mathsf{flipColumn}=\mathsf{false},\quad
\mathrm{anchor}=(\ell,1),\\
&\mathsf{transpose}=\mathsf{false},\quad
\mathsf{flipRow}=\mathsf{false},\quad
\mathsf{flipColumn}=\mathsf{true},\quad
\mathrm{anchor}=(r',w).
\end{aligned}$$
Thus the endpoint-role exhaustion itself is correct and dimension-independent. No small-width or small-height search is being used in that theorem.Required adapterThe formal declaration does not contain the physical phase labels, the transported tile partition, or port directions. In particular, phaseTenAtForcedPoint is a newly defined proposition; the imported WidthSixBottomOwner file does not prove
$$\text{“the physical owner of }z\text{ is a phase10 }U\text{”}
\Longrightarrow
\texttt{phaseTenAtForcedPoint}\,(\ldots,z).$$
Nor does it formally derive the four blocker hypotheses from endpoint disjointness and the neutral01 contact.Therefore the universal physical claim should be stated with the following adapter made explicit:After normalizing a neutral01 contact and pulling a phase10  $U$ -owner of  $z$  back through its actual transported isometry, the transported partition parity implies phaseTenAtForcedPoint, and the four foreign endpoints imply the four blocker non-membership hypotheses.Without that lemma, the Lean theorem is valid but only conditional. This is the main reason for the REVISE verdict.The same issue applies to the physical interpretation “northward terminal with the other leg east.” The formal conclusion gives the canonical endpoint and orientation bits; the port-direction interpretation is supplied by the external geometry convention and should be cited as an explicit adapter.2. The height collision is correctOnce the physical adapter is supplied, the height argument is valid.Let  $a$  be the active source’s incident height and  $h$  the incident height of the phase10 source owning  $z$ . In the normalized frame:the active inner bar row is  $2-a$ ;the active bar contains column  $0$ , because the near stem is in column  $-1$ , the other leg points east, and the width is at least  $6$ ;the phase10 owner has a collinear endpoint run on column  $0$ .The relevant endpoint run is
$$\{(t,0):-h\le t\le0\}.$$
Endpoint disjointness therefore forces
$$2-a<-h.$$
Equivalently,
$$a>h+2.$$
When  $a$  and  $h$  are even, this strengthens to
$$\boxed{h+4\le a}.$$
Consequently,  $a=4$  and  $a=6$  cannot support any legal phase10  $U$ -owner at the forced point, because every legal incoming height is at least  $4$ .The theoremleanincident_height_strictly_decreasescorrectly captures the arithmetic implication once disjointness has been reduced to the conditionlean¬ (-incoming ≤ 2-active ∧ 2-active ≤ 0)and the evenness assumptions are present.The iterated_descent_bound theorem is also arithmetically correct:
$$h_{i+1}+4\le h_i
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
h_i+4i\le h_0.$$
The note correctly warns that this is not a global mixed-chain termination result. A later continuation need not again be a phase10 owner at the same type of terminal. Phase10 corner ports and phase01 terminal ports are different geometric objects. That limitation is correctly stated and must be retained.Wording correctionThe sentence“ $F$ 's near stem contains every point  $(t,0)$  with  $-h\le t\le0$ ”is literally imprecise if “near stem” means only the canonical leg segment  $2\le r\le h$ . The endpoint at row  $-h$  comes from the transformed bar corner, while the remaining points come from the stem.Replace it with:The transformed collinear endpoint run, consisting of the bar corner together with the incident stem, contains every  $(t,0)$  with  $-h\le t\le0$ .The collision proof then uses the full endpoint predicate, exactly as required.3. The three-source family passes the arbitrary-parameter coordinate auditThe family is
$$\begin{aligned}
O_a&=U(14,a,4),
& (r,c)&\mapsto(r+2-a,c-1),\\
B&=U(6,4,4),
& (r,c)&\mapsto(c+1,5-r),\\
F_h&=U(6,h,4),
& (r,c)&\mapsto(r+1-h,c).
\end{aligned}$$
For the legal source model, the quantifier should be written explicitly as
$$\boxed{a,h\in 2\mathbb Z,\qquad h\ge6,\qquad a\ge h+4.}$$
The current wording emphasizes “even  $h$ ” but does not state equally clearly that  $a$  is even. The support parity table and the legal even-dimension source assumptions use  $a\bmod2=0$ . If odd  $a$  is intended to be included, that requires a separate proof; it cannot be inferred from the present table.After subtracting  $(1,1)$ , the endpoint sets are:
$$\begin{aligned}
E_O={}&
\{(1-a,c),(2-a,c):-1\le c\le12\}\\
&\cup\{(r,-1):3-a\le r\le1\}\\
&\cup\{(r,12):3-a\le r\le5-a\},
\end{aligned}$$

$$E_B=
\{(r,3),(r,4):1\le r\le6\}
\cup
\{(1,c),(6,c):0\le c\le2\},$$

$$\begin{aligned}
E_F={}&
\{(-h,c),(1-h,c):0\le c\le5\}\\
&\cup\{(r,0):2-h\le r\le0\}\\
&\cup\{(r,5):2-h\le r\le4-h\}.
\end{aligned}$$
These sets are pairwise disjoint for even  $h\ge6$  and  $a\ge h+4$ :the  $O$ -bar rows lie at or above  $2-a\le-h-2$ , while the  $F$ -bar is at rows  $-h$  and  $1-h$ ; $O$ 's near and far stems are in columns  $-1$  and  $12$ ; $F$ 's stems are in columns  $0$  and  $5$ ; $B$ 's occupied rows are  $1$  and  $6$ , with vertical bar columns  $3,4$ ;the only intended terminal-to-terminal neutral01 contact is  $O$ 's point  $(1,-1)$  with  $B$ 's point  $(1,0)$ .The three source matching unions are therefore disjoint because the endpoint sets are disjoint.4. The support table is correct, with two scope clarificationsThe support classes in the note agree with the exact transformed support predicates.The important cross-source classes are: $O$ 's inward near-stem supportsThese are
$$(r,0),\qquad r\text{ even},\quad 4-a\le r\le0.$$
For the subrange  $-h\le r\le0$ , the coordinate is an endpoint of  $F_h$ , hence it lies in  $P$  and is not retained as an exterior support.For earlier rows, parity gives
$$r\le-h-2,$$
because both  $r$  and  $-h$  are even. Those supports are separated from the  $F$ -bar rows  $-h$  and  $1-h$  by at least two rows, so no extra occupied neighbor appears. $F$ 's exterior near-stem supportsThese are the points
$$(r,-1),\qquad r\text{ even},\quad 2-h\le r\le0,$$
together with the bar-end support  $(-h,-1)$ . All lie on  $O$ 's collinear endpoint run in column  $-1$ , since
$$1-a\le-h-3.$$
They are therefore consumed by  $O$ 's endpoint set and are not retained.The two exceptional  $B$ -supportsThe support  $(1,-1)$  is an  $O$ -endpoint, and  $(0,0)$  is the forced  $F$ -endpoint. Both lie in  $P$ . The remaining  $B$ -supports have only their own source endpoint anchors.Remaining retained supportsThe  $F$ -inward supports
$$(r,1),\qquad r\text{ odd},\quad 3-h\le r\le-1$$
retain their unique  $F$ -endpoint anchor in column  $0$ . The nearest possible  $O$ -inward supports have even row and adjacent column, so they are diagonally separated; under the model’s cardinal support adjacency they do not create a selected-selected edge.The  $F$ -far supports in columns  $4$  and  $6$  are separated from all  $B$ -endpoints and  $B$ -supports by the  $h\ge6$  row gap. The  $O$ -outer supports in columns  $-2,11,13$  are separated from the other sources.Thus the table does give a complete all-parameter support argument, provided that:“consumed” is defined explicitly as “the support coordinate belongs to  $P$ , so it is excluded from the retained-support set”; andthe model’s adjacency convention is stated to be the cardinal one used by the interval arguments.The finite controls are only consistency checks. They are not needed for this conclusion.5. The forced full  $2+2$  receiver is realIn normalized coordinates,
$$p=(1,-1),\qquad q=(1,0),\qquad z=(0,0),$$
and the phase10 source also owns
$$w=(-1,0).$$
The forced tile containing  $z$  has corners
$$\{(-1,-1),(-1,0),(0,-1),(0,0)\}.$$
Its ownership is
$$\begin{aligned}
O_a&:\quad (-1,-1),(0,-1),\\
F_h&:\quad (-1,0),(0,0).
\end{aligned}$$
Therefore it is a genuine full  $2+2$  receiver.In the displayed, untranslated coordinates this is the tile with corners
$$(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1),$$
with  $O_a$  owning  $(0,0),(1,0)$  and  $F_h$  owning  $(0,1),(1,1)$ .The neighboring contact receiver contains the active and passive terminal points
$$p=(2,0),\qquad q=(2,1)$$
and retains the support
$$(3,0),$$
which is the normalized support  $(2,-1)$  of  $O_a$ .The phase10 source  $F_h$  maps its canonical terminal  $(h,1)$  to  $z$ , and its next collinear endpoint  $(h-1,1)$  to  $w$ . Hence  $z$  is a phase10 terminal, not a phase10 outer-corner singleton.Consequently,
$$z\notin P_{\mathrm{neg}},$$
where  $P_{\mathrm{neg}}$  consists only of original phase01 terminal singletons and phase10 outer-corner singletons. This directly refutes the candidate rule
$$\boxed{\text{full forced receiver}
\Longrightarrow
\text{forced point reserves a }P_{\mathrm{neg}}\text{ slot}.}$$
It does not refute the conditional implication
$$z\in P_{\mathrm{neg}}
\Longrightarrow
z\in E_{1\mathrm{reg}}.$$
The example is precisely outside the antecedent of that conditional statement.The sharpness claim is also valid: taking
$$a=h+4$$
realizes the smallest possible even height gap. The  $a=10,h=6$  instance is therefore a concrete sharp witness for the local  $+4$  separation.6. Scope that is correctly left openThe note is correct not to infer any of the following:a global mixed-chain termination theorem;a uniform coefficient-one bound;rectangular-grid triple equality;any improvement to the accepted global coefficient bounds;positive complete closed01 or AA coverage from the finite image controls.The  $a=10,h=6$  instance has the stated local counts: $78$  endpoints; $39$  source matching edges; $27$  retained supports;all  $78$  endpoints frozen; $H=12$ ,  $R=6$ ,  $\mu=6$ ;ambient slack  $96$ .Those values are valid for that witness. They should remain explicitly marked as instance data. They must not be presented as formulas for all  $a,h$ .Likewise, the finite control showing  $384$  complete isometry/phase images and  $96$  full forced receivers is a sanity check only. It is not the all-parameter proof; the interval/support argument is the proof.7. Declaration-count correctionThe supplied Lean file contains:one new def, phaseTenAtForcedPoint;six new theorem declarations.Thus it has seven new named declarations if definitions are counted, or six new theorem declarations if the helper definition is intentionally excluded. The provenance statement should say which convention is being used.Final dispositionREVISE.The coordinate mathematics supports the claimed local theorem and the sharp complete-family counterexample. The required revisions are:explicitly prove or cite the adapter from physical phase10  $U$ -ownership and transported partition parity to phaseTenAtForcedPoint;explicitly derive the four blocker hypotheses from the neutral01 contact and endpoint disjointness;state  $a,h$  as even legal dimensions in the family quantifier;replace “near stem contains  $[-h,0]$ ” by “the full collinear endpoint run, including the bar corner, contains  $[-h,0]$ ”;clarify “consumed,” cardinal adjacency, and the exact normalized support ranges;clarify the seven-versus-six declaration count.After those changes, and assuming the phase/port adapter is part of the already accepted geometric source theory, I would upgrade the mathematical result to ACCEPT.
